Job Description:

DataRobot delivers AI that maximizes impact and minimizes business risk. Our platform and applications integrate into core business processes so teams can develop, deliver, and govern AI at scale. DataRobot empowers practitioners to deliver predictive and generative AI, and enables leaders to secure their AI assets. Organizations worldwide rely on DataRobot for AI that makes sense for their business — today and in the future.

Our interns are not observers—they are contributors. Embedded in real teams and paired with dedicated mentorship, you will work on practical problems and deliver meaningful engineering output.

In this role, you will partner closely with our Documentation and Engineering teams to improve our developer-facing documentation platform, build CI/CD automation, and apply modern AI tooling to maintain freshness and accuracy. You will focus on building tools that minimize manual overhead—such as PR checks, content validation pipelines, and release workflows—helping our documentation evolve seamlessly alongside our product.

This is a fully remote position open to recent college graduates and early-career engineers. The program runs approximately 6 months.

What you'll do:




- Build CI/CD Checks & Workflow Automation: Develop lightweight GitHub Actions/PR checks to streamline doc reviews, run automated linters, and validate content changes against code updates.
- Automate Testing & Code Snippet Execution: Create automated tests that run documentation code examples and notebooks in CI to catch breaking changes early.
- Implement Content & Documentation Tooling: Assist in building tools and scripts to convert, generate, or publish documentation artifacts (e.g., Markdown/MDX pipelines, changelogs, and release summaries from Jira/PR data).
- Apply AI to Developer Tooling: Explore using LLMs and agentic scripts for practical site health tasks, such as flagging stale screenshots or enhancing doc indexing and retrieval for AI assistants.
- Collaborate & Document: Work closely with your mentor and docs engineers, communicate progress in weekly syncs, and present your accomplishments at the end-of-internship Showcase.


What you'll learn:




- CI/CD & Developer Productivity: Practical experience building GitHub workflows, PR bots, and test automation pipelines in a large-scale engineering environment.
- Modern Documentation Engineering: Hands-on experience with modern documentation frameworks (Markdown, MDX, static site generators) and API documentation lifecycles.
- Pragmatic AI & LLM Automation: How to apply LLMs, scripting, and evaluation to automate real-world maintenance tasks.
- Collaborative Software Engineering: Working in an async-first culture using Git, code reviews, Slack, and agile delivery practices.


Program Structure:

Phase I (Month 1) — Onboarding & Foundation: Learn the platform, toolchains, and repos. Co-create an Individual Learning Plan with your mentor and complete your first guided tickets.

Phase II (Months 2–5) — Core Project Delivery: Take ownership of scoped automation projects (e.g., CI testing of doc snippets, PR review gating, or generator scripts) with ongoing guidance and weekly 1:1 check-ins.

Phase III (Month 6) — Refinement, Handoff & Showcase: Finalize deliverables, write clean documentation for the team to maintain your work, and present your accomplishments at an Intern Showcase.

Qualifications:




- Recent graduate or completed Bachelor’s/Master’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or a related field (or equivalent practical project experience).
- Solid foundational programming skills in Python and comfort with scripting or data parsing.
- Familiarity with Git and GitHub workflows (branching, pull requests, code reviews).
- Basic exposure to or enthusiasm for CI/CD concepts (e.g., GitHub Actions) and web/documentation formats (Markdown, HTML/CSS, or JavaScript/TypeScript).
- Curiosity and eagerness to experiment with LLM APIs for developer productivity.
- Strong written communication skills and an organized, problem-solving mindset.


Nice to Have:




- Experience writing GitHub Actions or automating developer workflows.
- Prior experience with static site generators (Docusaurus, MkDocs, Next.js, etc.) or MDX.
- Familiarity with running automated tests or linting tools in CI pipelines.
- Personal or academic projects integrating LLM APIs (e.g., OpenAI, Anthropic, or open-source models).


The talent and dedication of our employees are at the core of DataRobot’s journey to be an iconic company. We strive to attract and retain the best talent by providing competitive pay and benefits with our employees’ well-being at the core. Here’s what your benefits package may include depending on your location and local legal requirements: Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance, Flexible Time Off Program, Paid Holidays, Paid Parental Leave, Global Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and more!

DataRobot Operating Principles:




- Wow Our Customers
- Set High Standards
- Be Better Than Yesterday
- Be Rigorous
- Assume Positive Intent
- Have the Tough Conversations
- Be Better Together
- Debate, Decide, Commit
- Deliver Results
- Overcommunicate


Research shows that many women only apply to jobs when they meet 100% of the qualifications while many men apply to jobs when they meet 60%. At DataRobot we encourage ALL candidates, especially women, people of color, LGBTQ+ identifying people, differently abled, and other people from marginalized groups to apply to our jobs, even if you do not check every box. We’d love to have a conversation with you and see if you might be a great fit.

DataRobot is proud to be an Equal Employment Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer. We do not discriminate based upon race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. DataRobot is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with physical and mental disabilities. Please see the United States Department of Labor’s EEO poster and EEO poster supplement for additional information.

Use of Artificial Intelligence in Our Hiring Process

These tools may assist in writing job descriptions, reviewing applications, assessing qualifications, and evaluating candidate materials. We're a global, team of innovators. Together, we harness engineering excellence and passion to co-create meaningful solutions to complex challenges. jd:
Job Description 
 About the Team:    
 GM’s Autonomous Vehicle Platform Software Engineering organization builds the foundational software that enables autonomous-driving capabilities to run reliably on production vehicle platforms. The organization’s teams span platform operating systems and compute drivers, embedded MCU software, core services and tools, and system-performance engineering. Their work includes developing low-level platform software, middleware, service interfaces, software-update and deployment capabilities, diagnostics, logging and observability, and performance tooling across vehicle compute systems.   
 Working at the intersection of software, hardware, AI/ML, and vehicle systems, the teams integrate operating systems, sensors, compute, and application workloads to deliver secure, efficient, testable, and production-ready autonomous-vehicle capabilities. Engineers collaborate closely with AV, AI/ML, hardware, systems, validation, and safety partners, with opportunities to contribute across embedded software, platform engineering, developer tools, and performance optimization. Depending on team needs, projects may focus on platform OS and drivers, MCU software, core services, vehicle software integration, or system and ML-workload performance.   
   
 About the Role:  
As an Autonomous Driving Software Engineer Intern, you will contribute to the design, development, and validation of cutting-edge software powering self-driving systems. You’ll collaborate with experienced engineers across AV Platform teams to build scalable, safety-critical software for autonomous vehicles operating in real-world environments. 
   
 What You’ll Do:   
 
• Develop, test, and deploy production-ready code across components of vehicle platform software.   
• Quickly ramp up on assigned codebase, product area, and/or system.   
• Complete assigned tasks efficiently with few iterations.   
• Identify problem statements, outline optimal solutions, account for tradeoffs and edge cases   
• Participate in design reviews, code reviews, technical discussions, and continuous integration and deployment practices.   
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams including hardware, systems, test, and safety to ensure seamless software integration.   
• Communicate effectively across multiple stakeholders.     
 Required Qualifications:    
 
• Currently enrolled in a full-time, degree-seeking program and in the process of obtaining a Bachelor's or Master's degree in computer science, artificial intelligence, machine learning, robotics, engineering, or a related STEM field.   
• Must be graduating between December 2027 and August 2029 and have at least one additional quarter/semester of school remaining following the completion of the internship.   
• Availability to work full-time, 40 hours per week, during the 12 week summer internship period between May 24th – August 13th or June 14th – September 3rd  2027   
• Strong foundation in algorithms and data structures, with proficiency in C++, Python, or another object-oriented programming language.   
• Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate across teams.    
 Preferred Qualifications   
 
• Demonstrated software engineering experience through an internship, work experience, coding competition, student engineering team or competition (e.g., SAE student competitions, EcoCAR, Formula SAE, or Baja SAE), research, coursework, or personal project.   
• Experience building, testing, and shipping production software, with exposure to safety-critical development (FDA, FAA, Automotive)   
• Familiarity with embedded build systems such as Yocto or Buildroot, networking fundamentals, and software integration across compute, MCU, and vehicle platforms.   
• Understanding of networking fundamentals relevant to embedded or distributed systems.   
• Experience with robotics frameworks (e.g., ROS), embedded Linux platforms, or common sensors (e.g., cameras, lidar, radar, IMUs) is a plus.   
• Passion for self-driving technology and its potential impact on the world     
 Compensation:   
 The compensation information is a good faith estimate only. It is based on what a successful applicant might be paid in accordance with applicable state laws. The compensation may not be representative for positions located outside of New York, Colorado, California, or Washington.   
 
• The salary range for this role is $8,100 – $10,300 per month. The actual base salary a successful candidate will be offered within this range will vary based on factors relevant to the position.    
• GM will provide a one-time lump sum taxable stipend payment to eligible students selected for the 2027 Student Program - to help facilitate administration of relocation benefits, please apply using the permanent address you would move from.     
 Work Arrangement:  
 Hybrid : This role is categorized as hybrid. This means the successful candidate is expected to report to their designated office three times per week, at minimum.    
   
 Location:   
 
• Sunnyvale, California   
• Warren, Michigan    



 About GM 
 Our vision is a world with Zero Crashes, Zero Emissions and Zero Congestion and we embrace the responsibility to lead the change that will make our world better, safer and more equitable for all.
 
 Why Join Us  
 We believe we all must make a choice every day – individually and collectively – to drive meaningful change through our words, our deeds and our culture. Every day, we want every employee to feel they belong to one General Motors team.
 
 Benefits Overview 
 From day one, we're looking out for your well-being–at work and at home–so you can focus on realizing your ambitions. Learn how GM supports a rewarding career that rewards you personally by visiting Total Rewards resources .
 
 Non-Discrimination and Equal Employment Opportunities (U.S.) 
 General Motors is committed to being a workplace that is not only free of unlawful discrimination, but one that genuinely fosters inclusion and belonging. We strongly believe that providing an inclusive workplace creates an environment in which our employees can thrive and develop better products for our customers.
 
 All employment decisions are made on a non-discriminatory basis without regard to sex, race, color, national origin, citizenship status, religion, age, disability, pregnancy or maternity status, sexual orientation, gender identity, status as a veteran or protected veteran, or any other similarly protected status in accordance with federal, state and local laws. 
 
 We encourage interested candidates to review the key responsibilities and qualifications for each role and apply for any positions that match their skills and capabilities. Applicants in the recruitment process may be required, where applicable, to successfully complete a role-related assessment(s) and/or a pre-employment screening prior to beginning employment. To learn more, visit How we Hire .
 
 Accommodations 
 General Motors offers opportunities to all job seekers including individuals with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation to assist with your job search or application for employment, email us or call us at 1-800-865-7580. In your email, please include a description of the specific accommodation you are requesting as well as the job title and requisition number of the position for which you are applying.

jd:
ABOUT PARSPEC

Founded in 2021, Parspec is revolutionizing the materials supply chain for the $13 trillion USD construction industry by digitizing and organizing the industry's product data. Our proprietary AI technology maintains a current and comprehensive catalogue of millions of products, enabling our customers to identify products that best meet their needs–instantly. Trusted by top designers, builders, distributors, manufacturers, and sales agents, and backed by leading venture investors, Parspec is paving the way for a more innovative, connected, and sustainable future in construction.

Join us in building transformative technology that reshapes one of the world’s oldest and largest industries.




THE OPPORTUNITY

We’re seeking an Applied AI Engineer Intern to join Parspec. This role is part of the AI team and works closely with Product and Engineering on fast-moving, real-world applications of AI.

As an intern, you’ll apply modern AI and machine learning techniques to concrete product problems, such as understanding product specifications, improving product recommendations, and exploring early agentic AI workflows, while learning how AI systems are designed, built, evaluated, and shipped in the real world.

This is an ideal role for a student who wants hands-on experience applying AI to complex, messy industry data and customer-facing product workflows.




WHAT YOU WILL ACHIEVE AND KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Contribute to AI-driven initiatives, from problem framing through experimentation and implementation

 - Build, prototype, evaluate, and iterate on models and AI-powered workflows used in customer-facing product features

 - Partner with Senior Applied AI Engineers and Product Managers to translate real customer problems into clear technical approaches and tradeoffs

 - Analyze structured and unstructured data (e.g., product specifications, documents, metadata) to improve model performance

 - Document assumptions, results, and learnings to support cross-functional alignment and decision-making


WHY THIS MATTERS

Construction remains one of the world’s largest and least digitized industries. Construction teams rely on manual workflows to interpret product specifications, identify suitable materials, compare options, and make procurement decisions. Parspec applies AI to power workflows that help stakeholders evaluate products, surface better options, and act with confidence. As an Applied AI Engineer Intern, your work will directly support these capabilities and the decisions they enable.




WHO YOU ARE

You’re excited about applying AI to real-world problems that don’t come neatly packaged. You enjoy breaking down complex systems, working with imperfect data, and experimenting to find practical solutions. You’re curious, technically grounded, and comfortable collaborating with Product and Engineering partners to balance model performance, system constraints, and customer impact.

Qualifications

 - Currently enrolled in a US-based, degree-seeking program (Bachelor’s, Master’s, or PhD) in Engineering, Computer Science, or related fields

 - Strong familiarity with core ML/AI concepts and tooling, such as model training(LoRA/QLoRA) and evaluation, embeddings, RAG systems, agentic frameworks like LangGraph, CrewAI or related techniques.

 - Strong familiarity with ranking and recommendations techniques.

 - Hands-on experience applying AI or machine learning to real-world projects, including working with imperfect data, making tradeoffs, and iterating based on results

 - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills

 - Ability to work effectively in ambiguous problem spaces with guidance and mentorship

 - Clear written and verbal communication skills for technical and non-technical audiences.

Preferred Qualifications

 - Exposure to B2B SaaS products, especially workflow-heavy or operations-focused software

 - Interest in or exposure to construction industry workflows, including materials procurement




WHAT WE OFFER

 - Competitive stipend for the duration of the internship

 - Hands-on ownership of meaningful product work that directly impacts customers

 - Mentorship from experienced Product, Design, and Engineering leaders

 - Flexible hybrid work environment to support both in-office collaboration and focused remote work

 - Exposure to a fast-growing AI-powered B2B SaaS company and real-world product decision-making

 - Opportunities for learning and professional development through regular feedback and collaboration


JOIN US AND LEAD THE TRANSFORMATION!

At Parspec, we recognize that traditional job descriptions don’t always capture the full range of your unique abilities—and that’s perfectly okay. You may not meet every requirement, but if you bring a mix of experiences, fresh perspectives, and a passion that aligns with our mission, we want to hear from you!

The Parspec team believes that varied backgrounds drive better outcomes and fuel innovation. We are a team of self-starters who lead from every seat. We think big, set a standard of excellence, and are committed to diversity and a discrimination-free workplace. We welcome applicants from all walks of life to join us and help shape the future of our industry.
fit_why: Applied AI intern fits his RAG/LLM work; lacks ranking/LoRA depth

Software Development Interns - Waterloo University 

 Remote - Winter Session 

 About Brave 

 Brave is on a mission to protect the human right to privacy online. We’ve built a free web browser that blocks creepy ads and trackers by default, a private search engine with a truly independent index, private AI assistant, latest privacy and security features, and a private ad network (opt-in!) that directly rewards you for your attention. Already over 120 million people regularly use Brave for a faster, more private web. Millions more switch every month.

 The internet is a sea of ads, hackers, and echo chambers. Big Tech makes huge profits off our data, and tells us what’s true and what’s not. Brave is fighting back. Join us!

 Brave is hiring 2 Software Engineer interns this fall from Waterloo University to assist adding AI, security and privacy features to our products. 

 Software Developer Co-op - Internship Role One 

 Contribute to the design, development, and maintenance of data-intensive systems and AI-powered services. 

 Key responsibilities include: 

• Build and maintain ETL pipelines for ingesting, transforming, and loading structured and unstructured data across internal systems 

• Develop backend services and tooling in Python and TypeScript to support data processing workflows and API integrations 

• Integrate and optimize LLM inference pipelines, including prompt engineering, model serving, and evaluation of large language model outputs 

• Deploy and manage containerized workloads on Kubernetes, including writing manifests, configuring autoscaling, and troubleshooting cluster issues 

• Collaborate with cross-functional teams to improve data quality, pipeline reliability, and system observability 
 
 Software Developer (Privacy) Co-op - Internship Role 2 

 Contribute to the design, development, and shipping of privacy and security features in the Brave browser (based on Chromium).

 Key responsibilities include: 

• Prototype, implement, and ship privacy-enhancing features end-to-end in C++ or Rust for the Brave browser 

• Build browser-native privacy protections privacy-enhancing permissions and anti-fingerprinting defenses 

• Navigate and contribute to an extremely large, complex codebase, applying knowledge of the Web security model and Chromium's architecture 

• Work with Web technologies (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) to develop and validate browser features 

• Collaborate async with a geographically-distributed, open source team using Git and GitHub 
 
 Working at Brave - What we offer 

• Ability to work remotely at an exciting and well-funded international startup headquartered in San Francisco 

• Cutting-edge technology, allowing you to work with state-of-the-art tools and software solutions 

• Competitive compensation of $6000.00 per month for 4 months. 

• Great international exposure and team atmosphere 
 
 If you are currently a student at Waterloo University, we would love to hear from you.  We offer flexible schedules to accommodate your studies.
fit_why: Role 1 fits backend/data; Role 2 is C++/Rust browser internals, no exposure

jd:
T-Mobile is synonymous with innovation–and you could be part of the team that disrupted an entire industry! We reinvented customer service, brought real 5G to the nation, and now we’re shaping the future of technology in wireless and beyond. Our work is as exciting as it is rewarding, so consider the career opportunity below as your invitation to grow with us, make big things happen with us, above all, #BEYOU with us. Together, we won’t stop!
 
 Get hands-on experience, training—and a leg up on a bright future.

T-Mobile didn’t become a leader by following the playbook. We got here by breaking it. We’re a disruptor that now plays on a higher tier, and we’re still raising the bar for millions of customers nationwide. If you want to work somewhere that sets the standard instead of matching it, this is your place. 

This is an 11-week paid learning experience where you’ll do real work, not busywork. You’ll build relationships with other interns and leaders across the company, and you’ll be paired with mentors who will challenge you to grow skills that matter. We’ll give you hands-on projects with real stakes, and we expect your creativity and sharp ideas to make an immediate impact. You’ll work alongside T-Mobile employees who have your back and who still believe the best ideas can come from anyone. 
 
 What It's Like: 
 Help shape how AI agents and developer tools can make software engineering at T-Mobile more effective. This internship focuses on the intersection of software engineering, large language models, and practical workflow automation. Work may span agent integrations, developer experience, testing, and evaluation, with an emphasis on reliable and maintainable solutions. You will collaborate with engineers to turn real workflow problems into working prototypes and use evidence to understand where AI helps and where human judgment remains essential. 

 What You'll Do: 
 Build a scoped AI agent or developer-tooling project that addresses a concrete engineering workflow. Implement integrations with approved APIs or tools, add automated tests and evaluation cases, and instrument the solution so its behavior can be inspected and debugged. Compare results against a baseline to assess correctness, usefulness, and failure modes. role: Machine Learning Intern - Generative World Models & Controllable Simulation
jd:
Waymo is an autonomous driving technology company with the mission to be the world's most trusted driver. Since its start as the Google Self-Driving Car Project in 2009, Waymo has focused on building the Waymo Driver—The World's Most Experienced Driver™—to improve access to mobility while saving thousands of lives now lost to traffic crashes. The Waymo Driver powers Waymo’s fully autonomous ride-hail service and can also be applied to a range of vehicle platforms and product use cases. The Waymo Driver has provided over ten million rider-only trips, enabled by its experience autonomously driving over 100 million miles on public roads and tens of billions in simulation across 15+ U.S. states.

 Software Engineering builds the brains of Waymo's fully autonomous driving technology. Our software allows the Waymo Driver to perceive the world around it, make the right decision for every situation, and deliver people safely to their destinations. We think deeply and solve complex technical challenges in areas like robotics, perception, decision-making and deep learning, while collaborating with hardware and systems engineers. If you’re a software engineer or researcher who’s curious and passionate about Level 4 autonomous driving, we'd like to meet you. 

 Waymo interns partner with leaders in the industry on projects that create impact to the company. We believe learning is a two-way street: applying your knowledge while providing you with opportunities to expand your skill-set. Interns are an important part of our culture and our recruiting pipeline. Join us at Waymo for a fun and rewarding internship!

 You will: 

• Design, implement, and scale controllable generation and test-time compute algorithms, multimodal conditioning, and critic-guided flow/diffusion steering—for foundation world models. 

• Investigate multimodal sensor + semantic latent conditioning, and representation alignment to advance toward holistic world simulation. 

• Leverage learned realism critics and agentic autoresearch workflows on large-scale TPU clusters to evaluate closed-loop interactive realism, long-tail scenario synthesis, and multimodal consistency. 

• Write clean, modular, and well-tested JAX code in core simulation and world-modeling codebases, collaborating closely with researchers across Sim Realism, Foundation Models, and Closed-Loop Training teams. 

 You have: 

• Currently pursuing a PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Robotics, or a related technical field, with an anticipated graduation date between December 2027 and August 2028 (returning to a degree program for at least one academic term after the internship). 

• Core Implementation Fluency (Mandatory): Strong tensor implementation and debugging skills in Python and JAX/Flax or PyTorch, with hands-on experience training and modifying modern neural architectures (such as Transformers, Diffusion/Flow-Matching models, or deep RL/critic networks). 

• Deep Research Expertise in Either: (a) Controllable Generative World / Sequence Modeling & Inference-Time Scaling (hands-on research experience in continuous flow matching / Rectified Flows, score-based diffusion guidance/steering, test-time compute / SMC, or parameter-efficient finetuning) OR (b) Multimodal Spatiotemporal Representation Learning & Closed-Loop Simulation (hands-on research experience in 4D/video tokenization, latent dynamics alignment such as REPA/DINO alignment, inverse RL / adversarial discriminators, or multi-agent trajectory modeling), with working familiarity in the other. 

 We prefer: 

• First-author publications at top-tier machine learning, computer vision, or robotics venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ECCV, CoRL, RSS, ICRA, or equivalent venues) in generative world models, flow/diffusion steering, controllable generation, or autonomous driving simulation. 

• Experience with multi-agent closed-loop simulation, counterfactual/adversarial traffic generation, or Sim2Real discriminator/critic stabilization (e.g., Waymax, WOMD, NuPlan, MGAIL, or reward-hacking mitigation). 

• Experience profiling and scaling distributed training and inference workloads on TPUs or multi-node GPUs (such as XLA compilation, vectorized batched rollouts, and memory optimization) and interest in external conference publication on Waymax/WOMD. 

 Note: This will be a hybrid onsite internship position. We will accept resumes on a rolling basis until the role is filled. To be in consideration for multiple roles, you will need to apply to each one individually - please apply to the top 3 roles you are interested in.
 
 The expected hourly rate for this full-time position is listed below. Interns are also eligible to participate in the Company’s generous benefits programs, subject to eligibility requirements.

 Hourly PhD Pay

 $85—$85 USD
fit_why: Requires PhD research in generative world models and JAX; candidate is undergrad

About Invesco 
 
 As one of the world’s leading independent global investment firms, Invesco is dedicated to rethinking possibilities for our clients. By delivering the combined power of our distinctive investment management capabilities, we provide a wide range of investment strategies and vehicles to our clients around the world. If you're looking for challenging work, intelligent colleagues, and exposure across a global footprint, come explore your potential at Invesco.

 What’s in it for you? 
 
 Our people are at the very core of our success. Invesco employees get more out of life through our benefit and perk offerings including: 
 
• Company networking events with other interns
 
• Peer Sponsor Program  
 
• Leadership Connection series
 
• Virtual Lunch and Learns
 
• Invesco Cares volunteer events
 
• Complimentary coffee and snacks
 
• 401(K) matching of 100% up to the first 6% with a discretionary supplemental contribution 

 Job Description 
 
 Ready to make your mark in the world of asset management? Spend an unforgettable summer at Invesco alongside a select group of high performing students. Our 9-week Summer Internship Program, kicking off in June 2027, offers you the opportunity to delve into the dynamic world of client services within a global investment firm. You’ll learn from seasoned professionals, gain hands-on experience, and build lasting connections.

 As part of our Summer Internship Program cohort, you’ll participate in orientation, networking events, development workshops, and volunteer activities. You’ll work side by side with talented teams to learn about the business and contribute to meaningful initiatives.

 Here’s the best part: crush your internship, and you could be eligible for a full-time offer to join our Early Career Program after graduation!

 What you can expect as a data science intern: 
 
• An introduction to Invesco Real Estate, its employees, history, philosophy, and all aspects of its business divisions by working alongside experienced professionals in their respective specialties. 
• Exposure to the complex real world of data science and analytics, how to navigate data challenges, create useful models, and learn the important skill of explaining data and models to business colleagues.  
• An introduction to private real estate investment, and how data science and analytics is integrated into the process.   
 Key Responsibilities: 
 
• Working with Data Scientists and Data Analysts to create value out of data. This could include: 
• Data Engineering: Helping with data querying, wrangling, transformations, exploratory data analysis (EDA), and feature discovery. 
• Statistical Modeling: Helping to create machine learning models for various finance & real estate use cases. 
• Data Visualization: Working on graphs, charts, BI tools, or other ways of displaying findings from models and research, ensuring they are useful to our colleagues. 
• Using data to help drive investment strategy. This could mean working on projects that impact: 
• Macroeconomic assumptions 
• Portfolio composition 
• Buy/Hold/Sell decisions 
• Market/Sector convictions 
• And more 
• Complete ad hoc analysis or work on longer term projects.  
 What you get  
 
• A Launchpad for Your Career  – Get ready to build real skills and set yourself up for a future at Invesco (and beyond).  
• Your Own Mentor  – You’ll be paired with a mentor who’s got your back, answers your questions, and helps you navigate your summer.  
• Intern Community  – Join a crew of fellow interns to collaborate, share ideas, and get to know—both in and out of the office.   
• Pathway to Future Opportunities  – Nail your internship, and you could be eligible for a full-time offer to join our Early Career Program after graduation!  
• Real Experience, Real Impact  – Work on meaningful projects, learn from our team, and see what it’s like to work at a global investment firm.    
 Minimum Qualifications   
 
• Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program in a data analytics, data science, or quantitative field and be a rising Junior graduating by summer of 2028 
• Minimum GPA of 3.2 on a 4.0 scale  
• Must be able to create data-driven insights using an analytical programming language (strong preference for Python) 
• Should have a strong desire to learn and grow; data science is an ever-evolving field 
• Critical thinking and creative problem-solving skills are crucial 
• Must be able to work well with a team; being positive and empathetic goes a long way 
• Strong analytical and quantitative abilities, organizational skills, and attention to detail 
• Interest in finance, economics, and capital markets 
• Strong leadership, initiative, and interpersonal skills; entrepreneurial and creative mindset 
• Ability to manage multiple projects concurrently 
• High energy with an ability to work in a fast-paced environment 
• Must be able to work from Invesco's Dallas office. 
• Must be authorized to work in the U.S. on a permanent basis. We do not offer any type of employment-based immigration sponsorship for this program. Invesco will not provide any assistance or sign any documentation in support of any other form of immigration sponsorship or benefit including optional practical training (OPT) or curricular practical training (CPT).  
• Relocation and housing will not be included if an offer is extended.    
 Preferred Qualifications   
 
• Demonstrated curiosity about real estate, finance, economics, and/or capital markets

It is not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities and qualifications required of employees assigned to this job. The job holder may be required to perform other duties as deemed appropriate by their manager from time to time. 
   
 Compensation for this position is $40/hr. 
 
 Full Time / Part Time 
 
Full time 
 Worker Type 
 
Student/Intern (Fixed Term) 
 Job Exempt (Yes / No) 
 
No 
 Workplace Model 
 
 Pursuant to Invesco’s Workplace Policy, employees are expected to comply with the firm’s most current workplace model, which as of October 1, 2025, includes spending at least four full days each week working in an Invesco office. This reflects our belief that spending time together in the office helps us build stronger relationships, collaborate more easily, and support each other’s growth and development.
